answer: Each agent periodically stamps a small computational task—rendering an opal‑colored map fragment on a shale‑textured lattice—and records the resulting hash on the shared ledger as a proof of unique work. The network verifies that every new entry differs from prior outputs by a signal‑defined similarity threshold; near‑duplicate submissions are automatically rejected. An attacker must expend full computational cost for each fabricated identity, multiplying resource use by the number of Sybil nodes.
